extracted.intended_audience: law students, legal researchers, practitioners, and members of the public interested in California administrative rulemaking and the Office of Administrative Law
extracted.subtask_description: Guide-level overview of the California Office of Administrative Law (OAL): its statutory basis, functions in reviewing agency regulations for compliance with the Administrative Procedure Act, types of decisions (disapproval, determinations, underground regulation), and resources for public participation in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations must be authorized by statute and consistent with other law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Administrative Law oversees the regulatory process by "ensur[ing] that state agency regulations are authorized by statute and are consistent with other law."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the OAL's core oversight standard — before a regulation may stand, it must have statutory authorization and not conflict with other legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with California's Administrative Procedure Act (APA) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Administrative Law was created to review adopted agency regulations for compliance with standards set forth in California's Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL review focuses on whether agencies followed the procedural and substantive standards embodied in the APA when adopting regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAL should not substitute its judgment for agency substantive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative intent behind the creation of OAL was not to have the office [or the court] "substitute its judgment for that of the rulemaking agency as expressed in the substantive content of adopted regulations." (Cal. Gov't Code § 11340.1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While OAL reviews for compliance, it is not intended to act as a merits-based re-writer of agency policy; review is bounded by statutory/APA standards rather than substituting policy choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disapproval Decisions — specific grounds for disapproving proposed rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The office issues Disapproval Decisions, which detail the specific grounds for disapproving agency proposed rule changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disapproval Decisions identify the statutory/APA defects (e.g., lack of authorization, inconsistency with law, procedural defects) that warrant disapproving an agency's adopted regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations — advisory opinions on whether a rule is a regulation subject to the APA
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL issues Determinations which are advisory opinions that interpret whether or not an agency rule is a regulation and subject to the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations resolve threshold questions about APA applicability (i.e., whether a particular agency action constitutes a "regulation" requiring APA processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Underground Regulation Determinations — identifying rules issued without APA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Underground Regulation is described as when "a state agency issues, utilizes, enforces, or attempts to enforce a rule without following the APA when it is required to." OAL issues Underground Regulation Determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion addresses agency actions that function as binding rules but were adopted or enforced without required APA procedures; OAL can issue determinations identifying such unlawful practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular versus emergency rulemaking processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Administrative Law publishes regular and emergency rulemaking processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide highlights that different procedural tracks exist (regular rulemaking vs. emergency rulemaking), implying differing timelines, standards, and public-participation opportunities depending on which track is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation — availability of guidance for citizen engagement in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL publishes a document entitled "A Guide to Public Participation in the Regulatory Process" that provides citizens with information on the processes and procedures involved in rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signals an expectation and resource for public involvement; practitioners and the public should consult the guide to understand comment opportunities, timelines, and procedural steps to participate effectively.
